headline: The December meeting is now a hike debate, not a cut debate — 10y at 5.10 with breakevens falling is a pure real-rate squeeze, and the AI complex is the collateral.
summary: Yesterday this was a dollar story. Today the bond market took it back. The rates composite deteriorated to -47 from -40: 2-year +13bp to 4.86 (+40bp on the week), 5-year +14bp to 4.95, 10-year +12bp to 5.10, 30-year 5.43. Crucially, the move is real, not inflationary — DFII10 +8bp to 2.86 and sitting 27.5% above its 200-day, while the 10-year breakeven is 2.24, -11bp on the month at the 19th percentile, and the 5-year breakeven is 2.30 at the 25th. Markets are not pricing a CPI panic; they are pricing a Fed that hikes again, with core CPI at z=0.93 and turning up (acceleration z=0.61) and fed funds already +25bp over three months to 3.88. That is the worst configuration for anything with duration in its cash flows.

The bill was paid in semis and crypto. AMD -8.8%, AVGO -4.8%, SOXX -3.7%, SMH -3.0%, NVDA -2.0% to a 0th-percentile 52-week reading and -26.4% on the month. Note the whipsaw: SOXX was +9.4% on the week, AVGO +18.2%, AMD +18.9%, MU +12.8% — a full week of rebound erased in one session, with SMH/SPY at z=-2.02 and still accelerating lower (acc z=-1.54). The factor damage is the real tell: growth/value is -10.7% on the month at z=-2.48 with acceleration z=-2.13, high-beta/low-vol -13.6% at z=-2.15, MTUM -2.0% today and -10.8% on the month. Crypto kept breaking: BTC -4.3% to 68,293 (-16.9% on the month), ETH 1,932 (-20.8%), SOL -25.7%, IBIT -3.5%, COIN -26.2% and pinned at the 0th percentile of its year. Same discount rate, same victims.

What did not break matters more. Credit tightened into an equity down day: HY OAS -10bp to 3.20, CCC -16bp to 13.14 — the first meaningful relief after +47bp on the month — IG -1bp to 0.89, BBB 1.11, HYG/IEF +0.1%, BKLN at the 97th percentile. Breadth actually reasserted after giving back yesterday: RSP/SPY +0.6% at z=3.11 with acceleration z=2.83, equal-weight +0.2% and the Dow +0.1% against NDX -1.2%. Financials are the cleanest beneficiary of a hike repricing — XLF +0.8%, z=1.28, acceleration z=1.55, 96th percentile, relative strength +9.8% on the month; KIE z=1.53; JPM +1.0%; 3m10y steepened 5bp. And the economy underwriting all of it is fine: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), capacity utilisation at the 100th percentile, growth pulse +2. This is a discount-rate event inside a healthy economy, which means dispersion, not de-risking — for now.

Two things argue the other way. First, the dollar is still the squeeze mechanism: DXY 103.41 at the 100th percentile of its year, EURUSD 1.105 at the 0th, USDCHF at the 100th, USDBRL +1.1% to 5.6407 with a 3.48 z-score and acceleration 2.71 — still the most extreme print on the board — though Brazilian equity is now diverging from it (EWZ +1.4%, Bovespa +0.7%). USDJPY 159.88 is in the intervention zone. Second, the industrial cycle flatly disagrees with hike pricing: copper -1.9% to 6.06 and -8.3% on the month, COPX -14.3%, FCX -14.7%, XME -6.1%, DBC z=-1.72. Gold is -5.4% on the month at the 0.2 percentile and silver -12.4% — zero-coupon assets cannot compete with 5%. Hedging demand is creeping back out the curve: VIX 19.3 (+3.2%), VIX3M 20.62 (+2.8%), term structure 0.936 turning up, MOVE 98.8 after +42% in three months. Own the cash-flow-now, short-duration side of the market and fund it with the long-duration side.

good.text: Credit refused to confirm the equity selloff: HY OAS -10bp to 3.20, CCC -16bp to 13.14 after a +47bp month, IG -1bp to 0.89, BBB 1.11, with BKLN at the 97th percentile and HYG/IEF +0.1%. Funding stress is not generalising.
Breadth re-accelerated after yesterday's wobble: RSP/SPY +0.6% at z=3.11 with acceleration z=2.83, equal-weight S&P +0.2% and the Dow +0.1% while NDX fell 1.2%. The index is being held up by the 493.

Financials are the direct beneficiary of hike repricing and a 5bp steeper 3m10y: XLF +0.8% at z=1.28, acceleration 1.55, 96th percentile and +9.8% relative strength on the month; KIE z=1.53, IAI acceleration 1.34, JPM +1.0%.

The labour and output data are not cracking: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, unemployment 4.1% and falling, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), industrial production +0.63, capacity utilisation at the 100th percentile.

Market-implied inflation is going the right way even as the Fed turns hawkish: 10y breakeven 2.24 (-11bp on the month, 19th percentile), 5y 2.30, RBOB gasoline -20.2% on the month. The hike is being priced against falling, not rising, inflation expectations.

Europe and India keep absorbing flows the dollar pushes out of weak EM: DAX at the 100th percentile (+6.0% on the month), CAC z=1.47 with acceleration 1.66, Sensex z=2.91, INDA +9.4% on the month at z=2.10.

bad.text: The entire Treasury curve repriced higher on a December hike: 2y 4.86 (+13bp, +40bp on the week), 5y 4.95 (+14bp), 10y 5.10 (+12bp), 30y 5.43. Rates composite worsened to -47 from -40.

It is all real yield: DFII10 +8bp to 2.86, 27.5% above its 200-day and at the 93rd percentile, while breakevens fall. Rising real rates with no inflation compensation is the purest valuation headwind there is.

Semis gave back a week in a day — AMD -8.8%, AVGO -4.8%, SOXX -3.7%, SMH -3.0%, NVDA -2.0% at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range and -26.4% on the month. SMH/SPY z=-2.02 and still accelerating down.
The long-duration factor unwind is accelerating, not stabilising: growth/value -10.7% on the month at z=-2.48 (acceleration -2.13), high-beta/low-vol -13.6% at z=-2.15, MTUM -10.8%, QQQ/SPY z=-1.92.
Crypto keeps leaking: BTC -4.3% to 68,293 and -16.9% on the month, ETH 1,932 (-20.8%), SOL -25.7%, IBIT -3.5%, COIN -26.2% at the 0th percentile, MSTR -22.1%. Same real-rate problem, more leverage.

The industrial cycle disputes the hike: copper -1.9% to 6.06 (-8.3% on the month, z=-1.39), COPX -14.3%, FCX -14.7%, XME -6.1%, DBC z=-1.72 — and the dollar keeps squeezing, DXY at the 100th percentile with USDBRL z=3.48 and still accelerating.

trades.name: Health care over semis
trades.line: Long XLV vs short SMH: the cleanest duration swap
trades.expr: Long XLV, short SMH, equal dollar weights. Scale the SMH leg into any one-day semi bounce of 3%+ rather than chasing weakness.
trades.thesis: A 5.10% ten-year with a 2.86% real yield reprices the longest-duration equity cash flows first. XLV earns now: relative strength +10.8% on the month, +16.3% on three months, z=1.94, 98th percentile, with LLY +19.4% on the month at a 52-week high. SMH is the opposite: relative strength -12.1% on the month, z=-1.72, rolling over, NVDA at the 0th percentile.
trades.trigger: Today AMD -8.8%, AVGO -4.8%, SOXX -3.7% wiped out a week in which SOXX was +9.4% and AMD +18.9% — the bounce had no legs, while XLV was +0.5% and XLP +1.4% on a down tape.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY reclaiming its 200-day (currently -9.6% below it) or XLV relative strength rolling from +10.8% to below +4% on the month.
trades.target: Another 10-12% of relative outperformance; SMH/SPY toward the 2024-style 0.58 area while XLV holds its 98th-percentile trend.

trades.name: Short long-end duration
trades.line: Short TLT into a December hike and rising term premium
trades.expr: Short TLT outright, or buy Dec/Jan TLT 78 puts. Size for a 4% adverse move; TLT 79.38 with the 20+ year ETF at the 24th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.thesis: The selloff is real-yield and supply driven, not an inflation scare — 10y breakeven -11bp on the month while DFII10 is +8bp today and 27.5% above its 200-day. A Fed that is hiking into 4.1% unemployment and 100th-percentile capacity utilisation removes the bull case for duration, and MOVE at 98.8 (+42% in three months) says the market has not finished repricing.
trades.trigger: 10y 5.10, 30y 5.43, 5y +14bp in a single session; TLT -3.1% on the week and -0.4% today with trend state down.
trades.stop: TLT +4% (10y back below ~4.90) or a jobless-claims break above 230k that puts cuts back on the table.

trades.name: Banks and insurers on hike repricing
trades.line: Long XLF + KIE: higher-for-longer with credit tightening
trades.expr: Long XLF 70% / KIE 30%. Add on any pullback toward XLF 56.5.
trades.thesis: Financials are the one sector where higher front-end rates are revenue, not a discount-rate penalty, and the credit backdrop is cooperating — HY OAS -10bp, CCC -16bp, BBB tightening — so the usual offset (loan losses) is not showing. XLF z=1.28 with acceleration 1.55 at the 96th percentile, KIE z=1.53 with acceleration 1.65, KRE/SPY +8.3% on the month.
trades.trigger: 3m10y steepened 5bp today and 2s10s +3bp while XLF rose 0.8% and JPM 1.0% on a day the Nasdaq fell 1.2% — the sector is leading on hike days, not just on cut days.
trades.stop: CCC spreads making new highs above 13.60 or KRE/SPY giving back the entire +8.3% monthly gain.
trades.target: +8% on the basket; XLF relative strength extending from +9.8% toward +15% on the month.

trades.name: Short crypto beta
trades.line: Short IBIT/COIN while real yields and the dollar rise
trades.expr: Short IBIT 60% / COIN 40%, or buy IBIT puts 1-2 months out. COIN is the higher-beta leg; keep it the smaller weight for borrow cost.
trades.thesis: Crypto is the purest long-duration, zero-cash-flow asset, and it is being hit by both channels at once: DFII10 at 2.86 and DXY at the 100th percentile of its year. BTC -16.9% on the month, ETH -20.8%, SOL -25.7%, ETH/BTC -4.8% — internal leadership is deteriorating, which is what sustained liquidation looks like rather than a flush.
trades.trigger: BTC -4.3% today to 68,293, breaking 70k; IBIT -3.5% and -15.8% on the month; COIN -26.2% on the month and at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.stop: BTC closing back above 75,000 or DXY breaking below 102.
trades.target: BTC 58-60k; roughly 20% on the short basket.

trades.name: Energy over copper miners
trades.line: Long XLE vs short COPX: cash flow now vs cycle later
trades.expr: Long XLE, short COPX, equal dollar weights. Can substitute XOM/CVX for half the long leg to reduce refining beta.
trades.thesis: Both are 'commodities', but one is a short-duration cash machine and the other is a levered bet on a cycle the data says is weakening. XLE is 10.4% above its 200-day with +8.4% three-month relative strength; COPX is 16.3% below its 200-day, -14.3% on the month, with copper itself -8.3% and rolling over at z=-1.39 and FCX -14.7%.
trades.trigger: Today XLE +1.0%, OIH +1.7%, CVX +1.6%, XOP +0.9% with WTI turning up at 88.92, while copper fell 1.9% and COPX 2.5%; copper/gold -2.0% on the day.
trades.stop: Copper reclaiming 6.40 / COPX back above its 200-day, or Brent breaking below 90.

trades.name: India over broad EM
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EEM: dollar-resilient EM
trades.expr: Long INDA, short EEM, equal dollar weights — strips out the Brazil/Korea/Taiwan drawdowns while keeping EM beta roughly neutral.
trades.thesis: The dollar at a 19-month high is picking off weak balance sheets and semiconductor exporters, not all of EM. INDA is +9.4% on the month at z=2.10 with acceleration 1.96 and +11.6% relative strength; the Sensex z=2.91. EEM is dragged by EWZ (-24.4% on the month), EWY (-10.7%), EWT (-12.2%) and KWEB (-6.4%), all of which are either currency-stressed or semis-levered.
trades.trigger: USDINR -1.3% on the month and rolling over at z=-1.44 — the only major EM currency strengthening against a DXY at the 100th percentile — while USDBRL printed another +1.1% at z=3.48.
trades.stop: USDINR breaking above 96 or INDA relative strength fading below +4% on the month.

trades.name: Fade the homebuilder squeeze
trades.line: Short ITB: the mortgage-rate tailwind just reversed
trades.expr: Short ITB, or buy 1-month ITB puts. Half size given the strength of the move; add above 96.
trades.thesis: Homebuilders rallied on a mortgage rate that fell 29bp over the month (acceleration z=-2.36) — but that series is dated 12 November and lags a 10-year that just added 26bp in a week to 5.10. The underlying demand data is still deteriorating: housing starts -5.2%, permits -0.4% and both in downtrends, consumer sentiment 48.1 and -7.0%.
trades.trigger: ITB +12.7% on the month with XHB/SPY at z=2.22 and acceleration 2.18 yet both trend states already read 'down'/'rolling over' — a counter-trend squeeze into a yield backup.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage printing below 6.90 or ITB closing above its 200-day with DHI confirming.
